smell: okd.WithEnv still encodes an order-dependency contract in New: WithEnv may construct the executor before WithLogger runs, and New compensates after the loop by re-applying WithLogger to the now-existing executor. Option functions should be commutative; any future lazy-building option (e.g. WithWorkDir) replicates the same dance.
severity_reason: The compensation works today but encodes a subtle ordering contract into New. Same pattern recurs in terraform.New (see related finding).
fix_summary: Defer executor construction until after the option loop: WithEnv stores pendingEnv []string on *Provisioner, then New builds p.executor = executor.New(executor.WithLogger(p.logger), executor.WithEnv(p.pendingEnv)) once. Options stay pure setters; the constructor owns ordering.
rule_source: Uber Go Style Guide §Functional Options (options should be commutative)
must_preserve: logutil.NopLogger default behavior and the 'env appended after os.Environ' semantics of executor.WithEnv.

smell: Phase NewOptions factory shapes still diverge across siblings. setup.DefaultOptions(projectRoot) takes ONLY projectRoot; install.NewOptions, postinstall.NewOptions, destroy.NewOptions take (cfg, projectRoot). install.NewOptions pulls eight fields from cfg; setup.DefaultOptions ignores cfg entirely, leaving the caller in okd.go to set up without cfg-derived defaults. Same-package verb; three different contracts.
severity_reason: Purely consistency. Callers hand-stitch the missing cfg plumbing for setup, which is exactly the job NewOptions does elsewhere.
fix_summary: Rename setup.DefaultOptions to setup.NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot) and fold any cfg-driven defaults into it. Matches the (cfg, projectRoot) signature the other three phase packages share. Single call site in okd.go.
rule_source: Uber §API Design (consistent constructor naming across sibling packages)
must_preserve: The setup Options zero-value behavior and any current setup-specific defaults.

smell: cleanup.Execute takes *Options whose zero Kind yields a bare '*errtypes.ConfigError{Msg: "unknown cleanup type: ..."}' with no sentinel callers can match. An Options{} zero-value (no Logger, no Kind) also silently defaults to NopLogger. Either make the zero value valid (default to Full) or reject nil/empty Kind up front with a named sentinel error.
severity_reason: Edge case — the three call sites (okd.go Prepare, destroy steps, standalone destroy) all set Kind explicitly. But the struct is exported with a zero-value footgun.
fix_summary: Add an exported `var ErrKindNotSet = errors.New(...)` sentinel and have Execute return it wrapped when opts.Kind == ''. Alternatively, switch to `NewOptions(kind Kind) *Options` so the required field is a constructor parameter, mirroring destroy.NewOptions / install.NewOptions.
rule_source: Uber §API Design 'make zero values useful or reject invalid construction'
must_preserve: All five Kind enumeration values (Full, WorkOnly, WebOnly, HAProxyOnly, TerraformOnly); Logger fallback to NopLogger.

smell: firewall.Configure and firewall.RemoveRules are exported but every in-tree caller uses ConfigureOKD / RemoveOKDRules. RemoveRules(HAProxyFrontendPorts(), ...) is the one exception — a single call in postinstall/haproxy.go:42. Configure has no direct caller. The pair is shaped like a 'future distro swap' API; flag as scaffolding, noting Configure is unreferenced.
severity_reason: Scaffolding-shaped: if Configure exists, RemoveRules stays; they map to a future 'configure arbitrary port set' CLI path (symmetric API).
fix_summary: Verify intent — are Configure/RemoveRules expected entry points for a future non-OKD distro? If yes, keep and document the layering. If no, inline Configure into ConfigureOKD and keep RemoveRules (still has one external caller).
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric API: Configure exists, RemoveRules stays)
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (package-level helpers live in producer pkg)
must_preserve: validatePort allowlist; both wrappers' current behavior.

smell: cleanup.GenerateSummary and cleanup.Summary struct are exported but the only caller is the package-private printSummary(). No external caller. The function is shaped like a public status-query but without a symmetric sibling (no cleanup.Verify or similar), so it does not cleanly fit scaffolding.
severity_reason: Possibly shaped for a future `okdctl cleanup status` CLI verb; defer to owner rather than deleting. No correctness impact.
fix_summary: Either unexport (GenerateSummary -> generateSummary, Summary -> summary) if no CLI surface planned, or keep both exported and add a one-line doc-comment pointing to the intended caller (e.g. 'used by okdctl cleanup status; see roadmap.md').
rule_source: Uber §Exported Surface ('do not export without a caller')
MEMORY.md §scaffolding (not symmetric — no matching verb in cleanup/)

fix_summary: Verify intent against roadmap.md — if a `okdctl releases latest [--minor N.M]` command is planned, keep both. Otherwise demote to private helpers. Do not delete without checking with owner.

smell: Phase.ValidateClusterAccess, Phase.SetupClusterAccess, Phase.SetupKubeconfig remain exported with callers only inside the same package's steps.go. Since Phase is itself exported and these are phase-public methods called by a user-facing okd.Provisioner, they fit a future-CLI-verb shape ('okdctl cluster access verify', 'okdctl kubeconfig-setup'). Flagged as scaffolding.
severity_reason: Scaffolding: shaped like future-CLI-verb (e.g. `okdctl cluster access verify`). Keeping per MEMORY.md §scaffolding.
fix_summary: Verify intent — do any planned subcommands call these? If yes, keep exported and document. If no, unexport (validateClusterAccess) to reduce package surface.

smell: terraform package still exports two constructors — New(workDir, opts...) and NewWithVarFile(workDir, varFile, opts...) — that differ only in one default. The second is a thin wrapper solely to preset VarFile. Idiomatic Go replaces this with a WithVarFile Option (already present-style in WithLogger/WithEnv/WithVerbose), keeping one constructor.
severity_reason: Clean constructor surface without functional change. Two constructors for the same type is the classic 'option drift' smell.
fix_summary: Add `func WithVarFile(path string) Option` that sets e.VarFile. Delete NewWithVarFile. Migrate the two call sites (install/workers.go:24 and infrastructure/proxmox/proxmox.go:125) to terraform.New(dir, terraform.WithVarFile(varFile), ...opts).
must_preserve: Default VarFile = workDir/terraform.tfvars when WithVarFile is not provided.

smell: Provider struct still has public methods (Connect, Disconnect, Provision, PlanOnly) but no consumer-side interface. cli/helpers.go and install/phase.go take the concrete *okd.Provisioner. If a non-Proxmox provider is ever on the roadmap, the Go idiom is to define the interface in the CONSUMER package (e.g. distribution.InfrastructureProvider), not the producer.
severity_reason: Not a defect today — Proxmox is the only supported infrastructure. Flag as guidance for the next provider.
fix_summary: If/when a second provider lands, define InfrastructureProvider interface in the distribution package (the consumer). Proxmox implements it structurally — no code change in proxmox/. Do NOT preemptively add the interface now.
must_preserve: No change today; this is a forward-looking note for when a second provider is introduced.

smell: cluster.NewK8sClient reads KUBECONFIG from os.Getenv at construction time, then builds the cmd runner. This couples the constructor to process env state at call time and means an Exec.Env mutation elsewhere (install.Phase.SetupKubeconfig appends KUBECONFIG= to Exec.Env) is NOT seen by a later-constructed K8sClient. The counter-comment at install/phase.go:147-150 still warns about this. Should either be documented as intentional or converted to lazy evaluation.
severity_reason: Documented footgun surfaces each time a new K8sClient is constructed post-SetupKubeconfig. Low chance of regression because call pattern is fixed today.
fix_summary: Move the os.Getenv('KUBECONFIG') read inside c.run — evaluate the env lazily on each exec.Run so a mid-process KUBECONFIG mutation IS seen. Alternatively drop the env fallback and require WithKubeconfig explicitly. Either way, delete the 'warning comment' at install/phase.go:147-150.
rule_source: Uber Go §API Design (no surprising late-binding on constructors)
must_preserve: The 'oc' over 'kubectl' fallback and the WithCLI/WithKubeconfig/WithLogger options.

smell: phase.ExternalToolBinaries has one in-tree caller (cleanup/packages.go:52). Exported for the sole purpose of avoiding a setup→cleanup import. Still sits in phase/paths.go when it really exposes a property of setup (what setup installed), not of the phase base type.
severity_reason: Low cost; the name is fine and the single-caller path explains why it is exported. Might still benefit from a dedicated file so setup.go doesn't have to grep phase/paths.go.
fix_summary: Move ExternalToolBinaries to a new phase/tools.go with a one-line doc clarifying 'these binaries are installed by setup; cleanup removes them.' No callsite change.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (shared cross-phase helpers live in phase/)
Go proverb: 'clear is better than clever'
must_preserve: The list of binaries (yq, helm, sops) and the cleanup caller.

smell: Step / Skipper / FatalChecker / StepCallbacks remain four interfaces that ProvisioningStep always composes together. The builtStep impl implements all four. The Orchestrator never accepts a bare Step or bare Skipper — it only accepts ProvisioningStep. Four interfaces where one (or two) would serve; none are consumed at the bare type by non-test code.
severity_reason: Not a correctness issue. The split is load-bearing ONLY if the orchestrator (or a future consumer) will accept a bare Step. Today it does not.
fix_summary: Keep Step (the 'id+name+execute' core could plausibly stand alone). Inline Skipper, FatalChecker, StepCallbacks into ProvisioningStep directly. Net: three interface decls removed, callers unaffected. Alternatively, leave as-is if a future test helper wants to accept just Skipper — document that intent on each interface.
rule_source: Go proverb: 'the bigger the interface, the weaker the abstraction' (applies inversely here — the unnecessary fragmentation weakens code)
must_preserve: Skipper, FatalChecker, StepCallbacks semantic behavior (currently encoded on builtStep).

smell: setup.DefaultOptions continues the Default* naming pattern common for 'zero-arg constructor of a defaulted options struct'. Other phase packages use NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot). The same repo also has install.DefaultBootstrapTimeout (constant) — a reader can't tell whether Default*-prefixed symbols are values or functions at a glance.
severity_reason: Naming consistency. Rename to setup.NewOptions(cfg, projectRoot) and the three *Options factories all share the same name.
fix_summary: Rename setup.DefaultOptions -> setup.NewOptions; accept (cfg, projectRoot) and fold any cfg-driven defaults inside. Single call site in okd.go updates. Aligns with opt-inconsistent-cfg-opts finding.
rule_source: Go naming convention: `New*` for constructors; `Default*` for values

smell: K8sClient is used in monitor.go only for ApprovePendingCSRs. Rather than accepting a concrete *cluster.K8sClient in MonitorInstallation, the caller could define a tiny consumer-side interface `type csrApprover interface { ApprovePendingCSRs(context.Context) (int, error) }` at the install package. This would align with 'accept interfaces, return structs' and make MonitorInstallation testable without a real kubectl.
severity_reason: A tiny interface at the consumer would simplify a future test helper. Not a current bug.
fix_summary: Inside install package define `type csrApprover interface { ApprovePendingCSRs(ctx context.Context) (int, error) }`. Accept it as a parameter to MonitorInstallation, defaulting to NewK8sClient(...). In tests, pass a fake.

smell: dns.BuildConfigData, dns.ConfigName, and dns.WriteDnsmasqConfig remain exported with callers only inside the dns package. dns.GenerateBootstrapConfig has a single external caller in setup/steps.go:368. The remaining three helpers do not fit a symmetric Build/Read or ConfigName/Parse shape and are not shaped for a CLI verb — safe to unexport.
severity_reason: Not scaffolding-shaped — no matching Build/Read or ConfigName/Parse symmetry and no CLI-verb shape. Fine to unexport BuildConfigData, ConfigName, WriteDnsmasqConfig while keeping GenerateBootstrapConfig (has one external caller) and the Deploy* entry points.
fix_summary: Unexport: buildConfigData, configName, writeDnsmasqConfig. Keep GenerateBootstrapConfig, DeployBootstrap, DeployProduction, Setup, RestoreSystemResolver as the package's external API. Three helpers become package-private.
rule_source: Uber §Exported Surface ('do not export without a caller')

smell: WriteDnsmasqConfig now takes ctx and checks ctx.Err() at entry (progress from prior run), but still does not thread ctx into os.MkdirAll / system.WriteTempFile / system.CopyFile — the body advertises cancellation only via the entry-gate, not per-step. Either plumb ctx into the underlying helpers or select on ctx.Done between the steps.
severity_reason: Entry-check is a small improvement over the prior placeholder; the remaining gap (no per-step cancellation) is a stylistic nit on a fast local-FS sequence. Demoted from minor to suggestion.
fix_summary: Add `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err(); default: }` between the mkdir / WriteTempFile / CopyFile steps so a mid-op cancellation is honored. Alternatively accept the entry-check as sufficient and add a one-line comment explaining why later operations are not gated.
rule_source: Google Go Style Guide §Contexts ('I/O operations that may block should honor ctx')
must_preserve: The atomic-write semantics (temp file + copy), the .backup file preservation, and the validateConfigName regex.
